result.title: Whose Voice Survives the Summary? A Voice-Retention Audit of LLM Employee Listening
result.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at the 60th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences (HICSS 2027)
result.summary: Organizations increasingly route employee feedback to leaders through large language model (LLM) summaries, an unaudited layer that silences already-spoken voice. We introduce a Voice Retention / Representation Ratio metric for representational bias in summarization and apply it to a bilingual (English/German) corpus of 2,586 free-text responses from a global professional service company. First, employees supply criticism more reliably than praise (withholding praise is 82 times more common). Second, across 45 leader-summaries the pipeline filters by popularity, not sentiment: criticism survives, yet a concern voiced once is dropped 86% of the time, with short and German-only content lost on the same axis (theme retention 0.14 vs 0.74; German directional). Controlling for frequency, sentiment has no independent effect; the harm is prevalence-driven, which sentiment-only audits miss. A targeted prompt recovers only named themes. We contribute the metric, field evidence, and a disaggregated voice-retention card.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出「声音保留/代表比例」指标，对某跨国专业服务公司 2,586 条英德双语员工反馈经 LLM 摘要管道后的保留情况进行审计，发现摘要筛选由出现频率而非情感驱动，低频、短文本和纯德语文内容更易被丢弃。
AI.relevance_reason: 该审计对「哪些证据在压缩后被保留」的量化思路，可能启发 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与信息坍缩的度量；低频内容被丢弃的现象或可类比 latent 状态对细粒度视觉信息的保留失衡，需核查其指标能否迁移至多模态场景。
